title: Hong Kong Milk Tea with Evaporated Milk
summary: Black tea simmered strong and dark, strained a few times for a silky body, then finished with evaporated milk and a little sugar, served hot.
equipment: fine-mesh sieve or cotton tea sock

ingredients.item: strong black tea bags (English or Irish breakfast)

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring the water to the boil, drop in the tea bags and turn the heat to medium-low. Simmer for 6 minutes, until very dark and fragrant. The long simmer gives the strong, slightly bitter base the milk needs.

steps.title: Squeeze
steps.text: Lift the bags out, pressing them against the side of the pan to get every drop back in.

steps.title: Smooth
steps.text: Pour the tea through a fine sieve into a jug and back into the pan 2-3 times. This aerates it and gives the silky body that cafés get from a cotton tea sock.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the evaporated milk and sugar. Taste and add more of either; it should be the colour of milky caramel. Serve hot.

tips: Evaporated milk, not fresh milk, gives the rich, slightly cooked flavour.
Blend two black teas, such as Ceylon and Assam, for a café-style depth.
Swap the sugar for condensed milk for a sweeter, creamier cup.
storage: Keep unsweetened tea in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat it or serve it over ice. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
